summary: This work uses hybrid stabilizer-tensor network methods to simulate coherent crosstalk noise during syndrome extraction in surface codes, capturing non-Clifford noise dynamics inaccessible to previous classical simulations. The inclusion of coherence in the noise model increases logical error rates and lowers the code threshold compared to incoherent-only models.
motivation: Standard surface code analyses assume incoherent noise or perfect syndrome measurements, missing the coherent crosstalk that arises during multi-qubit syndrome extraction in realistic devices.
method: Hybrid stabilizer-tensor network simulation techniques are used to model coherent quantum crosstalk noise during the syndrome extraction process in surface codes, allowing classical simulation of previously intractable non-Clifford noise.
result: Coherent noise increases logical error rates and reduces the threshold for fault-tolerant operation; the spatial distribution of crosstalk noise quantitatively affects performance metrics.
